title: Hazardous Material/Hazardous Waste (HM/HW) Staff Noncommissioned Officer/Noncommissioned Officer (MGySgt to LCpl) FMOS, DC I&L #
raw_text:
19. MOS 8056, Hazardous Material/Hazardous Waste (HM/HW) Staff
Noncommissioned Officer/Noncommissioned Officer (MGySgt to LCpl) FMOS, DC I&L
#

    a. Summary. Hazardous material/hazardous wastes (HM/HW) Staff
Noncommissioned Officers/Noncommissioned Officers manage numerous aspects of
the unit HM/HW program. The primary areas of focus are distinguishing HM from
HW implementing hazard communication training programs, monitoring HM
inventory control procedures, maximizing source reduction, and monitoring HW
streams, proper storage, and prescribed disposal practices. HM/HW Staff
Noncommissioned Officers/Noncommissioned Officers will also supervise unit
operations to ensure compliance with environmental regulations and maintain
the unit's emergency response equipment and procedures. In some cases, the
HM/HW Staff Noncommissioned Officer/Noncommissioned Officer will serve as the
command representative for environmental issues, implement CGI checklists,
and develop unit level operating budget inputs.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must possess normal color vision.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Successful completion of an HQMC approved formal school(s) or
HQMC or MCI region-approved base/installation course(s) of instruction that
addresses the duties specified below and provides fundamental information on
the safe and proper management of HM/HW and associated facilities in
accordance with applicable federal, Department of Defense (DoD), Department
of Navy (DON), and Marine Corps requirements. Assignment of the additional
MOS must be endorsed by the unit commander and the installation Comprehensive
Environmental Training Education Program (CETEP) coordinator at the
installation to which the Marine is assigned. Regional CETEP Coordinators may
endorse MOS requests for Marines stationed at tenant commands owned by other
DOD organizations.

        (2) MOS 8056 qualifying courses must appropriately address the
following requirements to include, but not limited to:

            (a) The Resource Conservation and Recovery Act regulations 40 CFR
122, 262, 264, 265, and 279.

            (b) Hazardous Material Transportation Uniform Safety Act of 1990
regulations in 49 CFR 172.704(a)(1) and 172.704(a)(3).

            (c) Occupational Health and Safety Administration's (OSHA) First
Responder Operations level emergency response training as prescribed by 29
CFR 1910.120(q)(6)(ii).

        (3) The 8056 MOS is an essential skillset for the development of
numerous logistics, maintenance, emergency response, and facilities
personnel. The MOS demonstrates that the Marine has been trained in basic
knowledge regarding hazardous material and waste handling. Additional annual
training is required in order to maintain compliance with federal and state
regulatory requirements for hazardous waste handling positions, but is not
required to maintain the AMOS.




                                         3-471                    Enclosure (1)
 3149                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (4) Training courses may embed one or more of the requirements listed
in a-c above into a single course or multiple courses. 8056 MOS nominees must
receive endorsements from the installation or Marine Corps Installations
region Comprehensive Environmental Training and Education Program (CETEP)
Coordinator and unit commanding officer prior to forwarding the request to
HQMC (officers) and IPAC (enlisted) for entry.

        (5) Candidates for the AMOS must fill 45 days of On-the-job training
in a billet that addresses Hazardous Material/Hazardous Waste
responsibilities, e.g. assigned as Environmental Command Coordinator,
Hazardous Waste Handler, HAZMIN Center worker, exercise Hazardous Waste
Handler, duty at the installation Hazardous Waste section, 90-day site, or
TSDF, etc. Unit commanders will confirm the fulfillment of the on-the-job
training period prior to the MOS being awarded.

       d.   Duties

            (1) MGySgt to GySgt:

                (a) Distinguishes Hazardous Material (HM) from Hazardous Waste
(HW).

                (b) Supervises operation of unit level HW site.

            (c) Develops/Ensures maintenance of desktop procedures and
turnover folders.

            (d) Supervises and validates the maintenance of unit
environmental training records.

            (e) Conducts and participates in applicable multimedia
environmental inspections, audits, and evaluations.

            (f) Supervises and maintains unit level inspection records and
required follow-on corrective actions.

                (g) Monitors maintenance of unit level environmental publications
library.

                (h) Develops and implements the unit level spill contingency
plans(s).

                (i) Tracks and consolidates unit level HW disposal costs.

            (j) Identifies unit level environmental operations budget
requirements.

            (k) Identifies environmental training needs and associated budget
requirements.

            (l) Ensures HM/HW transportation requirements are in compliance
with local directives.

            (m) Develops and sponsors environmental standard operating
procedures, letters of instruction, and operations orders for field
operations at the unit level for tactical and garrison operations.

                (n) Conducts unit level environmental briefings.



                                        3-472                        Enclosure (1)
 3149                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (o) Serves as the unit point of contact for applicable
environmental issues.

                (p) Promotes pollution prevention.

            (2) SSgt to LCpl:

                (a) Distinguishes HM from HW.

                (b) Operates HW sites in accordance with applicable directives.

                (c) Maintains desktop procedures and turnover folders.

                (d) Maintains unit level environmental training records.

                (e) Maintains unit level environmental inspection records.

                (f) Maintains applicable environmental publications library.

            (g) Maintains unit level Hazardous Communication Standard to
include Material Safety Data Sheets and Hazardous Material Information
System.

                (h) Tracks unit HW disposal cost.

                (i) Executes unit level spill contingency plan(s).

                (j) Maintains unit level emergency response equipment.

                (k) Conducts applicable multimedia environmental inspections.

                (l) Maximizes unit source reduction.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Hazardous Materials Removal Workers 47-4041.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
